goal: Prevent peers from forcing massive memory allocation and slow deserialization with crafted witness stacks
Protect node resources against denial of service blocks and oversized transaction inputs or outputs
agreement: Unaddressed objection: VerifyWitnessProgram allocates 91 MiB on unknown witness versions (fametrano)
Objection answered: warns against wide code churn before abstracting transaction access (purpleKarrot)
Tested support: confirms reduced allocations and passing functional tests (Yudis-bit)
Broad concept approval across multiple contributors (furszy, 0xB10C, instagibbs, ismaelsadeeq, rkrux, w0xlt)

categories.name: p2p
why: P1 because network deserialization limits drop oversized messages and protect node memory early
Rejects overweight blocks and transactions before allocating storage for malformed peers

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because shared serialization primitives are hardened against vector pre-allocation attacks
Bounds allocations to what can physically fit in valid protocol messages

categories.name: validation
why: P1 because crafted 4 MB blocks can no longer tie up 180 MiB of memory and hundreds of milliseconds
Cuts worst-case block deserialization from 279 ms to 19 ms and peak RAM from 182 MiB to 7.8 MiB
